title: Huaynaputina erupts in Peru
summary: The volcano Huaynaputina in southern Peru began the largest eruption in recorded South American history, burying villages and spreading ash over Arequipa.
reason: Magma rising beneath the Andes, where the Nazca plate sinks under South America, built pressure until the volcano exploded.
significance: Its ash cooled the Northern Hemisphere and contributed to the famine of 1601 to 1603 in Russia.
